land.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina, under Akkadian governors (Lugal-ushumgal under Naram-Sin, Puzur-Mama under Shar-kali-sharri) until Puzur-Mama 'declared Lagash independent'
'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash' (Code of Ur-Nammu); Lagash became 'the largest and most prosperous province of the empire'

capitals.name: Girsu (Tello)
capitals.note: 'Girsu (modern Telloh), about 25 km (16 mi) northwest of Lagash' was the religious center of the state. Not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: Lagash, Girsu and Nina: 'Under Gudea, Lagash experienced a golden age, with seemingly considerable independence from the Gutians'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Lagash polity in the Gutian period. The pages give no border beyond the three cities; Gudea's claims on Anshan and Elam held no land.

ledger.note: 2164 BCE: Ur-Baba opens the Second Dynasty of Lagash. Puzur-Mama, governor under Shar-kali-sharri, 'later declared Lagash independent, though Dudu of Akkad still reported taking booty from there'; Ur-Baba 'r. c. 2164 – c. 2144 BC (MC)'; Gudea 'r. c. 2144 – c. 2124 BC (MC)', under whom 'Lagash entered a period of independence marked by riches and power'; Ur-Ningirsu II 'r. c. 2124 – c. 2119 BC (MC)'.

2110 BCE: Ur-Nammu of Ur takes Lagash. Nam-mahani 'r. c. 2113 – c. 2110 BC (MC)'; the Code of Ur-Nammu's prologue: 'He slew Nam-ha-ni the ensi of Lagash'. Lagash became an Ur III province under Ir-Nanna.

wars.name: Gudea's campaign against Anshan and Elam
wars.outcome: 'Although Gudea claimed to have conquered Elam and Anshan'; 'the main military exploit seems to have occurred in his Year 6' (c. 2139). No land held; the Lagash page: 'some military operations to the east against Anshan and Elam'.

wars.name: Ur-Nammu's conquest of Lagash
wars.outcome: Nam-mahani slain; Lagash annexed as a province of Ur.

certainty.note: A city territory of three towns; no line on any page.

sources.title: Lagash
sources.note: Akkadian governors, Puzur-Mama, Ur-Baba c. 2164, Gudea, Ur-Ningirsu II, Nam-mahani c. 2113–2110, the Code of Ur-Nammu line.

sources.title: Gudea
sources.note: Reign c. 2144–2124, title ensi, independence from the Gutians, Year 6, trade with Dilmun, Magan and Meluhha.

sources.title: Akkadian Empire
sources.note: Lagash under Gudea as an Akkadian successor; Dudu 2189–2168.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: Lagash's Second Dynasty from Ur-Baba (c. 2164) to Nam-mahani's death (c. 2110), independent of both the last Akkadian kings and the Gutians. Start year: the page's first Lagash II king, Ur-Baba; Puzur-Mama's earlier declaration of independence is undated and Dudu (2189–2168) still raided Lagash, so -2164 is used. Gudea's trade reached Dilmun, Magan and Meluhha and he 'claimed to have conquered Elam and Anshan' (Year 6), but no land was held. The rulers between Ur-Ningirsu II (to 2119) and Nam-mahani (from 2113) are not on the pages opened, so no ruler strip. Girsu and Nina are not in the gazetteer; Lagash is.
